# RegExp

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index.

**Coverage**: 14/15 (~93%) · **Strict Coverage**: 14/15 (~93%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

PCRE2-backed; `--static` linking works (verified on Linux, including a Docker `scratch` container — `docker/Dockerfile.regexp-test`). Full design: [TDD-00035](../tdd/TDD-00035.md) ([ADR-00114](../adr/00/ADR-00114.md)–[ADR-00120](../adr/00/ADR-00120.md)).

Matching follows the **ECMAScript dialect by default** ([TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md), [ADR-00206](../adr/00/ADR-00206.md)–[ADR-00208](../adr/00/ADR-00208.md); verified on Apple Silicon, pcre2 10.47). The whole-program `-regex=<mode>` flag selects fidelity: `ecmascript` (default — `es-unicode` matching plus a source-normalization pass, which rewrites `.` to ECMAScript's exact "any character except a line terminator" so it matches `\x0b`/`\x0c`/`\x85` as real JS does, and UTF-16 code-unit positions at every user-visible offset, as the string layer indexes ([ADR-01826](../adr/01/ADR-01826.md))), `es-unicode` (`PCRE2_UTF` code-point matching + `NEWLINE_ANY`, no normalization, byte offsets), `es-utf16` (`es-unicode` matching with UTF-16 code-unit positions at every user-visible offset — `str.search`'s return, `lastIndex`, a replace callback's `offset` — and no normalization), `es-ascii` (the option-level fixes only, byte matching — smallest/fastest for known-ASCII programs), or `pcre` (raw PCRE2/Perl semantics, no ES wrapping — an explicit opt-in for PCRE-only features, *not* a fallback). The `ecmascript` normalization pass covers only the `.` rewrite so far; the remaining sub-items (`\u{…}`/`\p{…}`, Unicode `\w`/`\s`/`\b`, Annex-B legacy octal escapes, exact `$`/`m`) are deferred and disclosed in Known limitations below.

## Known limitations

- **Dialect-mode caveats** (what diverges from ES, per mode — these residuals exclude the matching rows above from Strict Coverage; [TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md)/[ADR-00206](../adr/00/ADR-00206.md)–[ADR-00208](../adr/00/ADR-00208.md)):
  - **Every mode — no UTF-16 unit matching without the `u` flag.** PCRE2 matches UTF-8 by code point, so `.` takes a whole astral character (`/^.$/.test('😀')` is true, false in V8) and an empty match never falls between a surrogate pair's halves (`'😀'.replace(/(?:)/g, '-')` is `-😀-`, `-\ud83d-\ude00-` in V8).
  - **`ecmascript` (default) — `$`/`m` over-exclude three control chars.** `$`/`m` use `PCRE2_NEWLINE_ANY` and anchor at `\x0b`/`\x0c`/`\x85`, where ES does not — exact anchoring needs a further `$`-rewrite (deferred). The normalization pass does **not** yet handle `\u{…}`/`\p{…}` code-point escapes, ES Unicode `\w`/`\s`/`\b` semantics, Annex-B legacy octal escapes, or the `u` flag; a syntax error PCRE2 reports without a V8 counterpart keeps PCRE2's message (`x{99999999999}`, which V8 accepts, is "number too big").
  - **`es-unicode` (opt-in) — `.`/`$`/`m` over-exclude three rare control characters.** The newline convention is `PCRE2_NEWLINE_ANY`, the closest single PCRE2 convention to ES's exact line terminators `\n \r \u2028 \u2029`, but it additionally treats `\x0b` (VT), `\x0c` (FF), and `\x85` (NEL) as line boundaries — so `.` excludes them and `$`/`m` anchor at them, where ES does not. Use the default `ecmascript` (whose normalization pass fixes `.`) if this matters.
  - **`es-unicode`/`es-ascii` — offsets are bytes.** `str.search`/`lastIndex`/a replace callback's `offset` report byte offsets there, while `.length`/`.slice`/`.charCodeAt` index UTF-16 code units, so the two disagree over non-ASCII text. The default and `es-utf16` report code units.
  - **`es-ascii` — `.` matches `\r`.** With no compile context, PCRE2's default newline convention treats only `\n` as the line end, so `.` matches `\r` where ES excludes it. Deliberate: `es-ascii` is defined as option-bits-only. Use the default `es-unicode` (which excludes `\r`) if this matters.
  - **`pcre` — raw PCRE2/Perl semantics throughout.** The PCRE2-vs-ECMAScript divergences the ES modes correct (`$`/newline, unset backref, `\uXXXX` throw) all apply by design in this mode; it exists for PCRE-only features and pattern porting, not ES fidelity.
  - **`es-unicode`/`ecmascript` — `\w`/`\s`/`\b` are not Unicode-aware.** `PCRE2_UCP` is deliberately not enabled: its Unicode-property tables diverge from ECMAScript's (UCP `\s` matches U+180E, dropped as whitespace by ES in Unicode 6.3), and enabling it *lost* net conformance on `built-ins/RegExp`. So `\w`/`\s`/`\b` match the ASCII/PCRE-default set, not ES's Unicode definitions — the ES Unicode class semantics are deferred ([TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md)). Code-point `.` (from `PCRE2_UTF`) is unaffected and works.
  - **`u`(nicode) flag still not implemented in any mode.** `es-unicode`'s `PCRE2_UTF` gives it code-point matching, but `\u{…}` code-point escapes, surrogate handling, Unicode `\p{…}`/class semantics, and strict-syntax validation are Option C — the `u`/`d` flags remain out of scope (see the row above).
